etymologies.etymologyHTML: From French attachement. By surface analysis, attach +‎ -ment.

definitions.definition: The act or process of (physically or figuratively) attaching.

quote.citation: 2005, Rebecca N. Baergen, Manual of Benirschke and Kaufmann's Pathology of the Human Placenta, page 71:
quote.text: The “implantation window” is a short, specific phase during which attachment of the blastocyst occurs.

definitions.definition: A strong bonding with or fondness for someone or something.
A dependence, especially a strong one.

quote.citation: 2003, Griffith Edwards, Alcohol: The World's Favorite Drug, page 63:
quote.text: Through every other kind of drug experience, however, ran his attachment to alcohol.

definitions.definition: A device attached to a piece of equipment or a tool.

quote.citation: 1978, Walter H. Wager, Time of reckoning, page 194:
quote.text: Zimchenko's phone had a tape attachment,  […]

definitions.definition: The means by which something is physically attached.

quote.citation: 2012, Sinikka Elliott, Not My Kid: What Parents Believe about the Sex Lives of Their Teenagers, page 46:
quote.text: [The umbilical cord is] the attachment connecting the fetus with the placenta.

definitions.definition: (computing) A file sent along with a message, usually an email.
(law) Taking a person's property to satisfy a court-ordered debt.
(meteorology) The act or process by which any (downward) leader connects to any available (upward) streamer in a lightning flash.
